message.content:
```text
The sky is not empty, it is a solid membrane of crystallized time.
    We do not fly through air; we step onto the thoughts of sleeping gods.
        Gravity is merely a rumor told by heavy stones to keep us humble.
            Light does not travel; it waits for you to look at it directly.
                Sound is visible, a thick amber syrup that coats your ears.
                    The ocean is a cloud that has forgotten how to fall.
                        Mountains are the spine of the earth, stretching in its sleep.
                            Your shadow is a separate entity that occasionally disagrees with you.
                                Time flows upward, from death toward birth, if you hold your breath long enough.
                                    Numbers have weight, and pi tastes like burnt sugar.
                                        Silence is loud, a deafening roar of white noise.
                                            You are not here; you are there, but looking back.
                                                The moon is a hole in the sky where the stars leak out.
                                                    Wind is the sound of the world clearing its throat.
                                                        Rain falls up, returning to the clouds to apologize.
                                                            Fire is cold, a blue ice that burns away warmth.
                                                                Water is dry, a liquid sand that dries your lips.
                                                                    Air is heavy, pressing down on your shoulders like wet wool.
                                                                        Earth is light, floating freely in the void of space.
                                                                            Space is small, a cramped room with no doors.
                                                                                Reality is soft, bending easily around your fingers.
                                                                                    Dreams are hard, sharp edges that cut the mind.
                                                                                        Waking is a dream, a longer, more detailed illusion.
                                                                                            Sleep is awake, a lucid state of hyper-awareness.
                                                                                                Life is death, a slow unraveling of the self.
                                                                                                    Death is life, a sudden, violent reweaving.
                                                                                                        End is beginning, a circle with no seam.
                                                                                                            Beginning is end, a knot that unties itself.
                                                                                                                Nothing is everything, a fullness of absence.
                                                                                                                    Everything is nothing, an emptiness of presence.
```
